newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close off on CANTV jitters.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close off on CANTV jitters.

text.p: Market jitters over potential hiccups in the long-expected share offering of phone company CANTV rattled a day of thin trade in Caracas stocks, brokers said, although few investors doubt the sale will not take place.
"There's some disquiet that opposition party Radical Cause has criticized the sale," said Financorp broker Hector Perez. "But I'm sure the sale will still go ahead," he added.
The bolsa's 19-share index slipped 1.8 percent to close at 5,653.36 as 26 shares fell, four rose and nine closed flat.
Slim trade saw 12 million shares change hands worth two billion bolivars ($4.3 million). At these levels "the market's very sensitive to any rumor," said Jose Gregorio Tineo.

Benchmark stock Electricidad de Caracas lost 14.50 bolivars to end at 491.50, steel company Sivensa lost 8.00 bolivars to close at 350.00, while foods company Mavesa slipped 5.50 bolivars to end at 140.00 bolivars.
The government is due to sell its 40 percent stake in the partially privatized phone company in November.
